lines.quote: Angry, divided, and dejected: the GOP blame game has begun; the defeat has turned into distancing the party from some of Trump's views — with no clear idea how to move on, with him or in spite of him
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek): the vehicle is the party's mood — three adjectives before a noun; the object is not in the door
lines.zWhy: a party blaming itself after the vote is the price's verdict, read as a mood

lines.quote: two years ago a sweep of the popular vote and seven battleground states left Republicans confident, 'even arrogant', of their grip through the second term; on Tuesday the voters who returned him made clear they are 'through with MAGA'
lines.note: the frame: the verdict as a mood, dated against 2024
lines.zWhy: voters 'through with MAGA' is the price's verdict without the price

lines.quote: the White House mood bleak Wednesday; aides expected to lose but not this badly ('a person familiar'); Talarico by double digits in Texas; South Carolina's senator beaten by a first-time candidate; a Kansas Senate seat flipped for the first time since 1932
lines.note: the count — the page's record line, with one anonymous source and three linked results
lines.zWhy: a count of flips in deep-red states is the vote in against the price

lines.quote: a 'circular GOP firing squad' is forming over what went wrong and how to rebuild
lines.note: the vehicle, named — the page's highest line after the hed
lines.zWhy: a firing squad over what went wrong is the verdict's aftermath, not the verdict
